items.prompt: A book costs Rp12.500. Rina pays with a Rp20.000 note. How many rupiah is her change?
hints: Take the price away from Rp20.000.
Count up from 12.500 to 20.000.

items.prompt: Dino pays exactly Rp10.000 using only Rp5.000 notes and Rp2.000 notes. How many different ways can he do this?
hints: Try 0 notes of Rp5.000 first. Then 1 note, then 2 notes.
With 1 note of Rp5.000, Rp5.000 is left. Can Rp2.000 notes make Rp5.000?
With 2 notes of Rp5.000, nothing is left.
items.explanation: With no Rp5.000 note, 5 notes of Rp2.000 make Rp10.000. With one Rp5.000 note, Rp5.000 is left, which two-thousand notes cannot make. With two Rp5.000 notes, it is exact. So there are 2 ways.

solution.say: With no Rp5.000 note, 5 notes of Rp2.000 make Rp10.000.
With one Rp5.000 note, Rp5.000 is left, which two-thousand notes cannot make.
With two Rp5.000 notes, it is exact.

items.prompt: A book costs Rp7.500. Mum buys 3 books and pays with a Rp50.000 note. How many rupiah is her change?
hints: Find the cost of 3 books first.
Take that away from Rp50.000.
items.explanation: 3 books cost 3 x 7.500 = Rp22.500. The change is 50.000 - 22.500 = Rp27.500.

items.prompt: A notebook costs Rp3.500 and a pen costs Rp2.000. Mia buys 4 notebooks and 3 pens. How many rupiah does she pay?
hints: Find the cost of the notebooks and the cost of the pens.
4 notebooks cost Rp14.000.
3 pens cost Rp6.000.
items.explanation: 4 notebooks cost 4 x 3.500 = Rp14.000. 3 pens cost 3 x 2.000 = Rp6.000. In all, she pays 14.000 + 6.000 = Rp20.000.

items.prompt: Three friends share the cost of a gift for Rp18.000 equally. Ana has already paid Rp5.000. How many more rupiah must Ana pay?
hints: Find how much each friend pays.
Take away what Ana has already paid.
items.explanation: Each friend pays 18.000 / 3 = Rp6.000. Ana has paid Rp5.000, so she must pay Rp1.000 more.

solution.say: Ana has paid Rp5.000, so she must pay Rp1.000 more.

items.prompt: Tono saves Rp2.500 each week. In how many weeks will he have Rp15.000?
hints: Count how many Rp2.500 make Rp15.000.
Two weeks make Rp5.000.
Rp15.000 is 3 times Rp5.000.
items.explanation: Two weeks make Rp5.000. Rp15.000 is 3 times Rp5.000, so it takes 3 x 2 = 6 weeks.

solution.say: Rp15.000 is 3 times Rp5.000, so it takes 3 x 2 = 6 weeks.

items.prompt: A shop says: buy 2 pens and get the 3rd pen free. Each pen costs Rp4.000. How many rupiah do 6 pens cost?
hints: Every 3 pens, one is free.
6 pens make 2 groups of 3.
How many pens do you pay for in each group?
items.explanation: In each group of 3 pens you pay for 2. There are 2 groups, so you pay for 4 pens. 4 x 4.000 = Rp16.000.

solution.say: In each group of 3 pens you pay for 2.
There are 2 groups, so you pay for 4 pens.

items.prompt: The notes and coins are Rp10.000, Rp5.000, Rp2.000, Rp1.000 and Rp500. What is the smallest number of notes and coins that make Rp18.500?
hints: Use the biggest note that fits first.
Rp10.000 first. Then Rp8.500 is left.
Keep using the biggest one that fits.
items.explanation: Take Rp10.000. Rp8.500 is left. Take Rp5.000. Rp3.500 is left. Take Rp2.000. Rp1.500 is left. Take Rp1.000. Rp500 is left. Take Rp500. That is 5 pieces.

items.prompt: A shirt costs Rp15.000 more than trousers. Together they cost Rp75.000. How many rupiah does the shirt cost?
hints: Take away the extra Rp15.000.
Share 60.000 equally to find the trousers.
items.explanation: Take away the extra: 75.000 - 15.000 = 60.000. The trousers cost 60.000 / 2 = Rp30.000. The shirt costs 30.000 + 15.000 = Rp45.000.

figure.alt: One Rp5.000 note, three Rp2.000 notes and four Rp500 coins.

hints: Add the notes first.
Three Rp2.000 notes make Rp6.000.
Add the Rp5.000 note and the four Rp500 coins.
items.explanation: The Rp5.000 note is Rp5.000. Three Rp2.000 notes are Rp6.000. Four Rp500 coins are Rp2.000. In all, 5.000 + 6.000 + 2.000 = Rp13.000.
